div.head: VI As 8.4
div.ab: Et si uestigium minetur ab una scyra in aliam, excipiant hoc qui propiores (proximiores) aderunt et educant illud uestigium; uel indicetur preposito: et ipse postea suscipiat cum monicione sua et minet uestigium illud extra scyram suam, si possit; si non possit, reddat ipsum pecus uno gildo. Et habeant ambe prepositure placitum hoc (questionis huius) in communi, sit alterutrum quod sit, sic a septentrionali merca sic ab australi: semper de scyra in aliam (scyram) omnis prepositus adiuuet alium ad pacem omnium nostrum per regis ouerhyrnessam.

⁊ gif man spór gespirige of scyre on oðre, fon þa menn tó þe þar nycst syndon ⁊ drifan þæt spór, oð hit man þam gerefan gecyðe: fó hé syððan tó mid his monunge ⁊ adrife þæt spór út of his scíre, gif he mage; gif he þonne ne mæge, forgylde þæt yrfe angylde. ⁊ habban þa gerefscypas begen þa fullan spæce gemæne, si swa hwær swa hit sy, swa be norðan mearce swa be suðan: á of scire on oðre þæt ælc gerefa fylste oðrum to ure ealra friðe, be cynges oferhyrnesse.

⁊ gif man spór gespirige of scyre on oðre, fon þa menn tó þe þar nycst syndon ⁊ drifan þæt spór, oð hit man þam gerefan gecyðe: fó hé syððan tó mid his monunge ⁊ adrife þæt spór út of his scíre, gif he mage; gif he þonne ne mæge, forgylde þæt yfre angylde. ⁊ habban þa gerefscypas begen þa fullan spæce gemæne, si swa hwær swa hit sy, swa be norðan mearce swa be suðan, á of scire on oðre—þæt ælc gerefa fylste oðrum to ure ealra friðe, be cynges oferhyrnesse.

And if anyone traces a trail from one district to another, the men who are nearest shall take up the trail, follow it until it can be brought to the notice of the reeve. Afterwards, he, with the men under his jurisdiction, shall take up the trail and follow it, if he can, to the boundary of his district. If, however, he cannot, he shall pay the value of the cattle, and the whole case shall be undertaken by the authorities of the two districts in common wheresoever it may happen that a trail passes from one district to another, whetherto the north or the south of our borders — all reeves shall help one another to maintain the security upon which we are all dependent or pay the fine for insubordination to the king.

And if one follows a trail from one shire into another, the men who are nearest are to take up and follow the trail, until it is announced to the reeve; he then is to take it up with [the men of] his district, and follow the trail out of his shire, if he can; if, however, he cannot, he is to pay the price of the cattle, and the two reeves’ districts are to have the full suit in common, no matter where it is, whether north of the boundary or south; so that even from one shire to another each reeve is to help the next for the sake of the peace of us all, on pain of the [fine for] disobedience to the king.

Und wenn man die Spur [verlorenen Viehs] von einer Grafschaft in die andere verfolgt, so sollen die Leute, welche dort zunächst wohnen, [sie] aufnehmen und die Spur verfolgen, bis man es dem [Grafschafts]vogt künde: der nehme sie dann mit seinem Bezirk[svolke] auf und leite die Spur aus seiner Grafschaft hinaus, wenn er kann; wenn er [das] aber nicht kann, bezahle er das Vieh mit einfachem Ersatz. Und es erhalten beide Sheriffsämter [das, wo Eigenthümer wohnt, und das des Spurendes] die ganze Klagesache gemeinsam, sei es, wo immer es sei, entweder nördlich der Grenze [unserer Grafschaft] oder südlich: dass immer aus einer Grafschaft in die andere jeder [Grafschafts-]vogt dem anderen helfe zu unser aller Polizeiordnung bei [Strafe der Busse für] Ungehorsam gegen den König.

And if the track [of lost cattle] is followed from one shire into another, then the men who live nearest there are to take [it] up and follow the track until it is reported to the [shire-]reeve: let him then take it up with the [people of his] district and lead the track out of his shire, if he can; but if he cannot [do that], let him pay for the cattle with single compensation. And both sheriffdoms [that where the owner lives and that where the track ends] are to have the whole suit in common, wherever it may be, whether north of the boundary [of our shire] or south: so that always from one shire to another every [shire-]reeve help the other for the peace of us all, on [pain of the fine for] disobedience to the king.
div.note: i.e. where the owner lives, and where the trail has ended
